title: Extension of a surjective integral morphism from an open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U\subseteq S$ be open [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $V\to U$ be a surjective integral morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there exists a surjective integral morphism $\overline V\to S$ such that $\overline V\times_S U$ is isomorphic to $V$ over $U$.

proof.text: The map $V\to U$ is affine because it is integral. Cover each affine $W\subset S$ by affine opens and refine $W\cap U$ by principal affine opens $W_i=D(f_i)$; write $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $g^{-1}(W_i)=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Apply the localization-compatible affine-chart construction of [lem-trf-open-relative-normalization-gluing], whose chart identifications are exactly the integral-closure localization statement [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. On an overlap the identifications localize to the same integral closure, hence satisfy the cocycle condition. The affine schemes obtained from these charts therefore glue (first over the affine cover of $W\cap U$, then over the affine cover of $S$) to a scheme $V'$ with an integral morphism $V'\to S$; by construction its restriction to $U$ is $V$. This is the arbitrary-open gluing argument in the proof of Stacks Lemma 0CNX, and it never treats the composite $V\to U\to S$ as a quasi-compact or quasi-separated normalization input.

source.place: Tag 0CNX proof; repaired by the arbitrary-open gluing lemma and Morphisms Tags 035F, 035H, 035K

proof.text: Let Z=(S\setminus U)_{\mathrm{red}} be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the complement. The existence, reducedness and underlying closed subset of Z are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its closed immersion Z→S is integral by the affine definition: on an affine open it is induced by a quotient ring map, hence an affine integral map.

Set $\overline V=V'\amalg Z$ and let q:\overline V→S be induced by the two structure maps. A finite coproduct of affine morphisms is affine; on an affine open of S its section ring is the product of the two section rings, and a product of rings integral over the base is integral coordinatewise. Therefore q is integral, using the definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and the coproduct construction [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The image of V' contains U because its restriction there is V→U, which is surjective, while the image of Z is S\setminus U. Hence q is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0CNX proof; definition of integral and surjective morphisms; Schemes Tag 01JB

proof.text: Base change of the coproduct along U→S gives (V'\amalg Z)×_S U ≅ (V'×_S U)\amalg(Z×_S U). The second summand is empty because Z is supported on S\setminus U, and the first is V by Step 1. Thus q^{-1}(U)=\overline V×_S U is canonically isomorphic to V over U, as required. This is the fibre-product definition [def-pc-fibre-product] together with the universal property of the coproduct.
